summary: Copies composited sprite pixel data into destination buffers through per-object sprite descriptors, advancing the animation frame when the current copy line reaches the buffer limit.

local_names.v2: frame copy state (this+0x184, sprite buffer/line array)

If this+0x120 (a1[72], sprite object count) is zero, skip per-object processing.
If this+0x120 (a1[72]) is greater than zero, enter the per-object allocation loop.

Iterate v23 over the descriptor-pointer array at this+0x124 (a1+73) for a1[72] objects; for each, call the vtable function at a1[1]+32 (this+0x4) with the object buffer v2[*(*v23+4)+18], the descriptor width *( *v23+12 ) scaled by a1[32] (this+0x80), the raw width, and 1; store each result in v14.
Indirect call through the vtable pointer at this+0x4 (offset 32) dispatches per-object sprite buffer setup.
Walk the line pointer i from v2[6] (this+0x19C) up to v2[7] (this+0x1A0), advancing one dword per iteration.
If the line pointer reaches the end bound (v2[7], this+0x1A0), increment a1[32] (this+0x80) and check it against a1[70] (this+0x118).
If the incremented frame index reaches the frame limit, call the frame-complete callback through the vtable at a1[99]+12 (this+0x18C) and return 4.
Otherwise call SpriteFrameSelector(a1) to advance to the next sprite frame and return 3.
If the copy position v2[5] (this+0x198) is below the scan-line limit a1[77] (this+0x134), keep copying; otherwise reset v2[5] to 0 and continue.
Per descriptor, only copy rows when the descriptor field at +56 (this+0x124 object row count) is greater than zero.
Compute the starting row offset v16 = (v17 * descriptor+52) << 7 where descriptor+52 is the row stride (this+0x124+0x34).

For each descriptor in the this+0x124 array, copy v9=descriptor+52 elements per row into the v2 line buffer (starting at &v2[v22+8]), writing v10 and advancing it by 128 each element; repeat for descriptor+56 rows.
Indirect call through the vtable at a1[101]+4 (this+0x194) checks whether the buffer is ready; if it returns false the copy loop exits.
After a full line, increment the copy position v5; when it reaches a1[77] (this+0x134) the copy position is zeroed and the next line pointer is taken from the loop state.
On normal completion store the final line pointer into v2[6] (this+0x19C) and the copy position into v2[5] (this+0x198), then return 0.
Return 0 on normal completion, 3 after advancing to the next sprite frame, or 4 when the frame animation limit is reached.
